pull_quote: Allowing difficulty to be our teacher.
bio_short: Cary Keishin Brief guides practice in the Theravāda tradition, rooted in the Buddha's early teachings. The Sit Raleigh community meets weekly for sitting meditation, dharma talks, and the kind of open inquiry that both challenges and comforts. We meet in person as well as on Zoom.
bio_full:
Cary Keishin Brief has been practicing and teaching in the Theravāda Buddhist tradition for many years. He founded Sit Raleigh to offer accessible, donation-based practice to anyone in the Triangle area, regardless of background or experience.

The teachings are offered by dana — generosity — so that the Dhamma remains available to all.

Individual mentoring in both meditation and practice study is available - please send a message by email to discuss possibilities. 

Cary currently is a chaplain at Wake Med Cary and at the Granville Correctional Institution in Butner, NC.  Prior to serving at Wake Med, Cary served as the Buddhist Chaplain at Duke University, guiding the Buddhist Meditation Community at Duke, Resident Chaplain at Rex and Chaplain Intern at UNC Chapel Hill.

Cary's Buddhist Chaplaincy training was with Roshi Joan Halifax and Upaya Zen Center Buddhist Chaplaincy Program in Santa Fe, NM. [](www.midtownmag.com/a-quiet-revolution-in-raleigh/)
